proof.criterion: No start or keeper lowers a deployed byte limit: an operator's raise of a full stream's limit stands, a lower one is raised to the setting
proof.surface: Real envoy-listener binary running against three nats-server v2.15.1 processes clustered on loopback, read with natscli v0.5.1
proof.observed: With the listener at ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES=44023414784 running, an operator raise to 50 GiB (53687091200) stood 40 s with no keeper write; an operator lowering to 1000000 was put back to 44023414784 by the keeper ('restored="max_bytes 1000000 -> 44023414784"').
proof.negativeControl: At 40e1a16643ee the tester saw the keeper put a raised limit (200000) back to 20000 about 33 s after the raise (round-3 test.json); here the lowered limit 1000000 is the control that the keeper still restores the floor

proof.criterion: A retry of a publish a full clustered stream refused is never acknowledged as stored when the server holds no copy
proof.surface: The bus's real publish path and async window against an in-process three-server nats-server v2.10.29 cluster (the server where the duplicate is staged; v2.15.1 does not stage it)
proof.observed: Refused with ErrStreamFull when full; both retries (Publish and the window) return ErrNotStored, still after a purge; after a stream leader step-down both are stored with Sequence > 0 and their Nats-Msg-Id.
proof.negativeControl: With either guard removed the retry returns nil while the stream does not hold the message, and the test fails ('... succeeded and the stream does not hold its message')

proof.criterion: Earlier proofs still hold: raise to three copies, limit, DiscardNew and id kept across listener and Dispatch starts; a full stream refuses and keeps what it holds
proof.surface: Real envoy-listener and envoy-dispatch binaries against three nats-server v2.15.1 processes and one standalone v2.15.1 server
proof.observed: P1 R1 -> 3 current peers, limit 44023414784, discard new, one id, durable at 3; P2 unchanged at setting 1; P3 Dispatch restores subjects 5 -> 8 keeping copies, limit and id; P4 10 of 30 publishes acknowledged, 20 refused 'maximum bytes exceeded (10077)', messages 1-10 kept.
proof.negativeControl: Standalone v2.15.1: ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS=3 -> exit 1 naming ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS=3; ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES=44023414784 on a 29 GB store -> exit 1 'insufficient storage resources available'; ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS=0 refused at load
